title: A goal can rest without quitting
description: Pausing a goal deliberately, with a date to revisit it, is different from drifting away from it — and much kinder.

body.heading: Not every season suits every goal
paragraphs: There are seasons of life — a new baby, a demanding project, an illness in the family, exams — when some goals simply cannot get air. Pretending otherwise does not protect the goals. It just adds guilt to an already full season.
Resting a goal is the honest alternative: a conscious decision that this goal is paused, on purpose, for now. Nothing is being failed. Something is being sequenced.

body.heading: Rest it properly
paragraphs: Write down three things: the goal, why it is resting, and the date you will look at it again — a month or a season ahead, in the calendar, not in your head. That date is what separates resting from quitting.

If the goal has a tiny maintenance version, you can keep the thread warm at almost no cost: five minutes a week, one page, one small transfer. If even that is too much this season, let it rest completely. A clean rest restores better than a guilty trickle.

body.heading: Wake it gently when the date comes
paragraphs: When the revisit date arrives, look with fresh eyes. Sometimes the season has changed and the goal fits again, usually smaller than before. Sometimes you realise the goal belonged to an older version of you, and releasing it is the right ending.
Either way, you decided. Goals that are rested and revisited stay yours. Goals that are silently abandoned have a way of haunting — and they do not have to.

takeaway: Pause on purpose, write the revisit date, and let the goal sleep without guilt.
